- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.22) within 3–5 days, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; for 30-day forecasts, smooth transitions using 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted price changes.
- When sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.11), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–2% to account for latent market resilience.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is persistently negative; if sentiment turns positive after a drop, model should not immediately reverse direction.
